The **next TransLink departures** (bus, SkyTrain, SeaBus), the **SkyTrain line
status** and the **Mobi bikes** near your home, in Gladys.

This integration is not affiliated with TransLink nor with Mobi by Rogers.

## Get started in 3 steps

No technical knowledge is needed, and no account to begin with.

1. **Check the address of your house in Gladys**: _Settings → Houses_. The
   house must have a position on the map. The integration uses it to find the
   stops near you. The position stays in your Gladys.
2. **Install the integration** from the integration catalog, and accept the
   access to the house location. Open its configuration page and press
   **Save**, without filling anything in.
3. Open the **Discover** tab of the integration. The 3 stops and 2 Mobi
   stations closest to your home are offered there, with their name and the
   direction of their routes, e.g. "TransLink – Waterfront Station @ Bay 2 (50
   → False Creek South)". Press **Add** on each one you want.

That's it. You now get the **next departures** at each stop, and the bikes and
free docks of each Mobi station.

The message at the top of the configuration page always tells you what to do
next. For example: "Ready: 3 stops and 2 Mobi stations to add. Open the
Discover tab…".

Device names start with **TransLink –** or **Mobi –**, so they are easy to tell
apart in the device list of Gladys. You can rename them freely in Gladys.

A SkyTrain station is offered once, for all its platforms. Its bus bays ("Bay
1", "Bay 2"…) are stops of their own.

### Showing the departures on the dashboard

1. Open the dashboard, then press **Edit**.
2. Add a widget and choose **TransLink departures**.
3. Choose the stop, then save.

The **Mobi station** widget is added the same way. The **TransLink line
status** widget needs a TransLink key (see below).

Without a key, scheduled times carry a **~** and are grey: "~12 min" means
"scheduled in 12 minutes". Departures tracked in real time are green, without
a ~.

## Going official real time and adding the lines (optional)

Without a key, the departures come from Transitous, a free community service:
the timetable, and the real time where Transitous has it.

With a free, personal **TransLink API key**:

- the departures come straight from the **TransLink real-time feed**, updated
  every minute;
- the **TransLink – SkyTrain and SeaBus** device appears, with the status of
  the Expo, Millennium and Canada lines, the SeaBus and the West Coast
  Express.

### Getting the TransLink API key (5 minutes)

1. Go to the [TransLink developer portal](https://developer.translink.ca) and
   **create an account** (_Register_). Confirm the email you receive.
2. Log in: the page of your account shows your **API key**. Copy it.
3. In Gladys, open the configuration of the integration. Paste the key in
   **TransLink API key**, then press **Save**.
4. Press **Test the TransLink API key**. Both lines must show ✔.
5. Go back to the **Discover** tab and add the **TransLink – SkyTrain and
   SeaBus** device.

The labels of the portal may differ slightly.

**Requests.** One read of the TransLink feed serves all your stops: with the
default settings the integration makes about 2,200 requests a day, **whatever
the number of stops**. The message of the configuration page shows the
estimate for your setup.

## Watching other stops (work, school…)

For a stop far from home:

1. At the bottom of the configuration page, press **Find a stop**. Type a
   street, a station or the stop number, e.g. "Granville Station" or "Davie
   Bidwell".
2. The answer lists the stops with their number and the direction of their
   routes, e.g. `50040 — Waterfront Station @ Bay 2 (50 → False Creek South)`.
3. Copy the number (`50040`) in **Stops**, save, then add the stop in the
   **Discover** tab.

The number is also the one written on every TransLink stop sign ("Stop
#50040").

For Mobi stations, the **Find a Mobi station** button works the same way.

### Going further

The **Stops** field accepts several numbers separated by commas, a route
filter after `@` and a name after `:`.

| Entry                  | Meaning                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `50040`                | every route calling at stop 50040    |
| `61935@99`             | route 99 only                        |
| `61935@99\|14`         | routes 99 and 14                     |
| `61935@99:Bus to work` | route 99, displayed as "Bus to work" |

## What each device holds

**Stop:**

- **Next departure**, **Departure 2**…: the minutes to wait. 999 means no
  departure is scheduled.
- **Next departure route**…: the route ("99", "Canada Line").
- **Next departures**: a summary, e.g. `99 3 min · 14 ~11 min`.

**SkyTrain and SeaBus** (with a key): for each line, a **status** (`Normal`,
`Disrupted`, `Notice` or `Unknown`) and the **message** of the TransLink
alert. An alert about a single station (an elevator, an entrance, a bus bay)
does not change the status of the line.

**Mobi station:** the bikes (e-bikes included), the e-bikes, the free docks
and the state of the station.

A station that leaves the Mobi network shows 0 bikes, 0 docks and the state
"Removed from the Mobi network (seasonal?)", with an orange dot on the device.
It resumes by itself when it comes back.

## Scenes

**Triggers:**

- **Departure approaching**: a departure gets under 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 or 15
  minutes. Example: "when the 99 is 5 minutes away, turn the hall light on".
- **Line status changed**: a line is disrupted, gets back to normal, or
  receives a notice. Example: "if the Expo Line is disrupted, send me a
  message".
- **Mobi station changed**: the station runs out of bikes or docks, or gets
  some back.

**Actions:**

- **Read the next departures**: e.g. a message every morning "Your 99 comes in
  \{\{minutes\}\} minutes".
- **Read a line status**: returns the status, the TransLink message and
  `normal` (true or false).

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom                                | What to do                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "set the address of your house"                   | _Settings → Houses_: place the house on the map, then save the configuration of the integration again.            |
| "Gladys did not share the location of your house" | Reinstall the integration and accept the location access, or type stop numbers.                                   |
| Nothing in the Discover tab                       | Read the message of the configuration page: it says what is missing.                                              |
| "TransLink refused the API key"                   | Check the key on the developer portal, then paste it again.                                                       |
| "Stop … is not in the TransLink stop list"        | Check the number on the sign. A brand new stop comes with the next version of the integration.                    |
| Station "Removed from the Mobi network"           | The station left the Mobi network: it will come back by itself. To follow another one, see "Find a Mobi station". |
| A stop stays at 999                               | No departure scheduled (at night), or a route filter matching no route of the stop.                               |

## Privacy, data and licences

- The house location is only used to look the nearby stops up, in the stop
  list shipped with the integration: it is sent nowhere.
- Stop list: the TransLink GTFS, shipped with the integration (updated with
  every version).
- Departures without a key: [Transitous](https://transitous.org/sources/), a
  free community service, from the TransLink data.
- Real time and alerts: TransLink open data, under the TransLink
  [terms of use](https://www.translink.ca/about-us/doing-business-with-translink/app-developer-resources).
- Bikes: public GBFS feed of Mobi by Rogers.
- Integration code: Apache 2.0 licence.

Estos son los parámetros que TransLink Vancouver te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Get started in 2 minutes | `section` | No | 1. Check that your house has an address in Gladys (Settings → Houses). 2. Save this page. 3. Open the “Discover” tab of this integration and press “Add” on the stops and Mobi stations near your home. That's it: you get the next departures and the Mobi bikes right away. A TransLink key (optional, free) adds the official real time and the line status. |
| Near my home | `section` | No | How many of the closest stops (within 600 m) and Mobi stations (within 1 km) are proposed in the “Discover” tab. 0 turns the suggestion off. |
| Stops near my home | `number` | No |  |
| Mobi stations near my home | `number` | No |  |
| Real time and lines (optional) | `section` | No | Without a key you get the departures of the free Transitous service: the timetable, and the real time where Transitous has it. With a free TransLink key you get the official real-time predictions and the status of the SkyTrain lines. Getting one takes 5 minutes: follow the step-by-step guide. |
| TransLink API key | `secret` | No | The API key of your account on the TransLink developer portal. |
| Watch the lines | `boolean` | No | Creates a "TransLink – SkyTrain and SeaBus" device with the status of the Expo, Millennium and Canada lines, the SeaBus and the West Coast Express. |
| Departures without a key | `boolean` | No | Without a key, show the departures of the free Transitous service. |
| Other stops and stations (optional) | `section` | No | To watch a stop that is not near your home (work, school…): type its number, written on the stop sign, or find it with the “Find a stop” button at the bottom of this page. |
| Stops | `string` | No | Stop numbers. Optional route filter after @ and custom name after : — e.g. "50040, 61935@99:Bus to work". |
| Mobi stations | `string` | No | Mobi station ids, with an optional custom name after : — e.g. "0201:Station at home". |
| Advanced | `section` | No | The defaults suit almost everyone. With a TransLink key, one read of the real-time feed serves every stop. |
| Departures refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the departures are refreshed, in seconds. |
| Lines refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the line status is refreshed, in seconds. |
| Mobi refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the Mobi stations are refreshed, in seconds. |
| Departures per stop | `number` | No | How many upcoming departures each stop device exposes as features. |
| Language of the values | `select` | No | Language of the feature names and of the texts published. |

## Cómo instalar TransLink Vancouver en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: TransLink Vancouver aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-translink:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-translink](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-translink).

TransLink Vancouver requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

TransLink Vancouver es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
